To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) the use of a lexical repetition-based discourse segmentation model improves the topical make-up, readability, and cohesion of automatically generated text summaries, and b) the use of the same model as a filter for the input text to a summarizer, in conjunction with the dynamic adjustment of the summary size, improves the topical make up, readability, and coherence of the summaries generated.
(1) lexical cohesion is a useful factor in the development of document summarizers and (2) lexical repetition is a useful cohesive device in text.

(i) lexical cohesion can be utilized to enhance the quality of summaries, (ii) lexical cohesion can help to identify shifts in topic and thus can be utilized to segment documents, (iii) the integration of a lexical cohesion-based model of discourse structure with a linguistically-based model of summarization is a promising research direction, and (iv) lexical repetition alone can be utilized to improve the quality of summaries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: (1) The use of discourse segmentation for improving the quality of summaries.
the use of discourse segmentation as a tool for summarization.

the following issues: (i) the automatic identification of cohesive devices in texts, (ii) the automatic recognition of discourse segments in texts, (iii) the automatic identification and extraction of salient text units in texts, and (iv) the automatic generation of summaries from texts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of our initial experiment are encouraging and that the proposed framework is capable of producing summaries of better quality than a state-of-the art sentence-based summarizer, and that it has the potential to be further improved by the incorporation of other cohesive factors.

lexical repetition is indeed an important factor in discourse segmentation and document summary generation, and that it is possible to develop a system capable of utilizing this factor in order to generate better summaries.

the results obtained are very encouraging for the future of lexical cohesion in document summarization, but that further work is needed in order to achieve the same level of performance as that of sentence-based summarization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

lexical cohesion factors can be successfully integrated in the generation of summaries, and that the use of such devices is a viable approach for addressing problems related with coherence degradation, topical under-representation, and readability deterioration.

we have developed a framework which is capable of generating summaries that are more cohesive, more readable and more representative of the topics in the original document than those generated by state-of-the-art summarizers.
the use of lexical repetition as a discourse segmentation device can improve upon the quality of the summarization process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lexical repetition is a useful cue for detecting shifts in topic.
the use of a discourse segmentation model can improve the coherence of a summarization output, even if the summarizer is not explicitly designed to exploit cohesion information in the source text.
the use of lexical cohesion factors can be a powerful tool in the generation of more cohesive and more readable summaries.
